title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: S is a base with 2 invertible (to identify mu_4 with (Z/4)_S one needs i on S). X -> S is a P^1-bundle, and Delta ⊂ X is a relative divisor of degree 6, finite étale over S. Delta is assumed locally isomorphic to the standard configuration {0, ∞, 1, -1, i, -i} ⊂ P^1_S, the vertices of the octahedron. The previous page introduced the finite étale group scheme Gamma = Aut_S(X, Delta), locally isomorphic to (S_4)_S. Grothendieck wants a combinatorial 'scheme of octahedra' structure on Delta with Gamma = Aut^+_oct(Delta).

This page argues that an octahedral structure on a 6-element set is determined by its group of direct automorphisms.
- The three diagonals Delta_1, Delta_2, Delta_3 (pairs of opposite vertices) are the classes of the equivalence relation R: s ~ s' iff Gamma_s = Gamma_{s'}. Each isotropy group is cyclic of order 4 and fixes exactly the vertex and its antipode.
- The polyhedral structure is recovered from the partition Delta = Delta_1 ⊔ Delta_2 ⊔ Delta_3. The 12 edges are the 2-element subsets other than the Delta_i (15 - 3). The 8 faces are the 3-element subsets that are sections of Delta -> Delta/R (2^3).
- So an octahedral structure is the same as a fibrewise fixed-point-free involution, i.e. an étale equivalence relation of degree 2. Equivalently it is the same as the S_4-action of Gamma on Delta.

Consequences: an octahedral structure on Delta ⊂ X, if it exists, is unique, since it is read off from Gamma. Hence existence is local and descends.

The page then starts the check on the standard model X = P^1_S. The automorphisms fixing 0 and ∞ form mu_4 ≅ (Z/4)_S, generated by z ↦ iz, and by homogeneity the same holds for the pairs (1,-1) and (i,-i). The next page shows that the stabiliser of a non-diagonal pair such as {∞, -1} is trivial. It concludes that Gamma preserves the partition, so Gamma ⊂ Aut^+_oct(Delta), with equality because Aut^+_oct is generated by its three cyclic subgroups of order 4.

Purpose: this is a lemma in Grothendieck's treatment of elliptic-curve moduli in characteristic ≠ 2. The octahedral six-point configuration is, for instance, the cusp configuration of the genus-0 curve X(4), with PSL_2(Z/4) ≅ S_4 acting. Here it is used to rigidify the structure, i.e. to show the octahedral data is canonical and étale-local.
errors: Minor: the identification mu_4 ≃ (Z/4Z)_S presupposes a primitive 4th root of unity i on S, which is implicit since the model configuration contains ±i. Over a general S with 2 invertible one only has mu_4, and Delta is only locally (étale) standard.

Minor imprecision: 'automorphismes directs' of a combinatorial octahedron is not defined on this page. Inside the full group (Z/2)^3 ⋊ S_3 of order 48 there are several index-2 subgroups. 'Direct' is not the even permutations of the 6 vertices: a 90° rotation is an odd permutation. The correct one is the rotation subgroup, which is singled out here by Gamma itself.
Isotropy groups are those of Gamma acting on Delta. The phrase 'définie par la vérification s ↦ Γ_s' should read 'application s ↦ Γ_s'. No mathematical error otherwise.

ideas.what: Octahedral structure on a 6-point set recovered from the S_4-action: diagonals as classes of equal stabilisers (cyclic of order 4), edges and faces read off from the partition
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorics of the octahedral rotation group S_4; a 'scheme of octahedra' as an étale fixed-point-free involution on a degree-6 étale cover

ideas.what: Uniqueness of the octahedral structure on Delta ⊂ X implies the existence question is local (descent of a rigid structure)
ideas.modern_name: Étale descent for rigid structures / the octahedral divisor as a torsor under S_4
ideas.where_published: General principle in SGA1; this specific application is unpublished

ideas.what: Aut(P^1, {0,∞,±1,±i}) ≅ S_4 with vertex stabilisers mu_4, over bases with 2 invertible
ideas.modern_name: Octahedral subgroup of PGL_2; cusps of X(4), with PSL_2(Z/4) ≅ S_4
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein); X(4) cusp geometry is standard modular-curve lore

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, correct verification of classical octahedral combinatorics and a standard descent remark, carried out relative to a base S. No new result or unrecognised connection appears on this page.
